A record with source "council_compromise" is a ▌ the Council compromise text prints on a line of its own where it deleted a point, paragraph or passage: `follows` and `precedes` name the items it stands between ("after": at the end of the provision text, precedes null), and `page` and `source_url` the page of the Council document that prints it; the provision text carries no mark for it, and the Council prints no number for what it deleted. Mechanically derived from the source; not part of the legal text. Null means the release predates the record (see the typed warning), never that nothing was deleted.

changes.description: What KIND of change this comparison evidences, read off the same artefact as pairs[]. Types: paragraph_added, paragraph_deleted, paragraph_amended (with words_changed, counting both sides of a substitution), figure_changed (with from/to quoting the served text), heading_changed, the article_* counterparts of the first three for an article's text outside any numbered paragraph, and none_detected where nothing was found — never an empty list. An entry carries `paragraph` and, where the served text settles it, `point` and `subpoint`, in the §7 locator model's own field names; an article_* entry carries none of them. Those components are a CITATION, not a promise of retrieval: a sub-point is often not a block get_provision serves, so open an entry at the enclosing point, and then the paragraph, which does serve the text the entry quotes. A roman sub-point is always qualified by its letter point (PSR Art 97(2)(a)(ii), never (ii) alone), and a list the text does not settle is left unlocated. ARTICLE-SCOPED, not page-scoped: the whole inventory travels with every page of pairs[], so a client paging through must not concatenate it. Repeated identical entries are repeated occurrences in one paragraph, not duplicates. Null means this release predates the inventory, which is not the same as none_detected.

station_id.description: Station identifier — use this ID with data tools.

source.description: Data source: coops (CO-OPS) or ndbc (NDBC buoy).

type.description: The data capability this row leads with — always one of the values in capabilities. When a types filter of capability values is set this is the first requested capability the station has, so it never contradicts the filter; otherwise it is the first capability. Omitted when the station has no data capability (e.g. a bare buoy/fixed platform matched only by a platform filter) — read platform for its identity. This is a data-product axis, never the physical platform class.

platform.description: NDBC physical platform class: buoy, fixed, oilrig, dart, tao, usv, or other. A different axis than type/capabilities (which describe data products). Omitted for CO-OPS stations — CO-OPS publishes no platform taxonomy.

distance_km.description: Distance in km from the search center (only present when lat/lon search was used).

state.description: US state or territory code (CO-OPS stations only): the station's own catalog code, or — when its catalog rows carry none, as with every current station — the state of the nearest state-bearing CO-OPS tide or water-level station within 25 km, marked by state_derived. A derived state can be wrong on waters shared across a state or national border. When neither applies, the station's own non-code catalog value (e.g. FM) is shown as published and unmarked — no state filter returns such a station, since the filter takes codes only. Omitted when the station publishes nothing at all and no state-bearing station is that close.

state_derived.description: True when state was derived from the nearest state-bearing CO-OPS tide or water-level station within 25 km, because the station's own catalog rows carry no state code. Omitted when state is the station's own.

capabilities.description: Data products available at this station: any of tide, current, water_level (CO-OPS) or met, current_profile, water_quality (NDBC). Empty when the station reports no data capability — platform still identifies it.

prediction_class.description: CO-OPS TIDE-prediction class: reference (predicted from the station's own harmonic analysis, serving both hilo and the 6-minute curve) or subordinate (high and low events derived as offsets from a reference station, hilo only — noaa_marine_get_tide_predictions rejects interval="6min" for it). A third axis beside type/capabilities (data products) and platform (NDBC physical class). Omitted for a station with no tide-prediction row; a current station carries its class per bin in bins[], where subordinate means something different. An unrecognized catalog code is passed through verbatim.

reference_id.description: The reference station a subordinate tide station derives its offsets from — the station to request a 6-minute curve from. Omitted for a reference station and for any station with no tide-prediction row.

bins.description: Depth bins this current station publishes predictions for, in the order CO-OPS publishes them. Each bin has its own depth and prediction class, and its bin number is what noaa_marine_get_currents takes as bin. Omitted for a station with no current-prediction rows.

bin.description: CO-OPS bin number — pass it as the bin input of noaa_marine_get_currents. Omitting bin there selects the shallowest bin.

depth.description: Bin depth in FEET. The catalog publishes one figure with no unit switch, unlike the depth noaa_marine_get_currents echoes, which follows that call's units. Null when CO-OPS publishes no depth for the bin, which is usual where depth_type is U.

depth_type.description: CO-OPS depth-reference code as published: B, S, or U. A U bin usually carries no depth. Omitted when the catalog row has none.

prediction_class.description: CO-OPS prediction class for this bin: harmonic (predicted from the bin's own harmonic analysis) or subordinate (derived by offsets from a reference station) both serve the normal flood/ebb/slack series, while weak_and_variable may instead answer noaa_marine_get_currents with a coverage statement and no events, or report that no predictions are published at all. The class is per bin because one station can mix classes across its bins. An unrecognized catalog code is passed through verbatim.

items.description: One depth bin CO-OPS publishes current predictions for at this station, with its depth and prediction class.
A single station matching the search criteria.

stations.description: Stations matching the search criteria, sorted by distance (if lat/lon provided) or by exact ID match then name. Empty when nothing matched.

total_found.description: Total stations matching the filters before the limit was applied. Zero when nothing matched.

truncated.description: True when total_found exceeds the limit and not all matching stations are returned. Increase limit or narrow filters to see more.

applied_search.description: The narrowing dimensions this search applied, echoed when nothing matched so the caller can see which filter emptied the result.

catalogs_read.description: Catalogs this search actually fetched. Empty when source and state cancelled each other out and no catalog was read.

center.description: Proximity-search center, present only when latitude and longitude were supplied.

latitude.description: Center latitude the proximity filter used.

longitude.description: Center longitude the proximity filter used.

query.description: The name/ID substring as the server used it — trimmed and lowercased. Omitted when no query was supplied or it was blank.

radius_km.description: Radius bound in km, present only when a center was given. Applies whenever a center is present and defaults to 100 km.

source.description: The source filter applied: coops, ndbc, or all.

state.description: The state filter applied, matched against each station's resolved state: its own catalog code, or for a station publishing none the state of the nearest state-bearing CO-OPS tide or water-level station within 25 km. Restricts results to CO-OPS and excludes NDBC.

types.description: The resolved types filter. Omitted when no types filter narrowed the search.

items.description: A requested capability or platform filter value.

types_by_source.description: The requested types split by the source that can carry them — every value belongs to exactly one source, so a single-source types filter reduces the search to that source.

coops.description: Requested values only a CO-OPS row can carry.

ndbc.description: Requested values only an NDBC row can carry.

notice.description: Guidance about the result set: why a search matched nothing, which catalog did not answer, or that the list was capped.

sources.description: Which station catalogs were attempted, answered, and failed. Present only when a catalog fetch rejected, so a partial result set is never read as a complete one.

answered.description: Catalogs that returned a station list — the results cover these only.

attempted.description: Catalogs this search needed, after source and state decided which to read.

failed.description: Catalogs whose fetch rejected. A station served only by one of these is missing.

Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

gt.description: Great diurnal range, MHHW − MLLW (GT), in the requested units. A difference between two tidal planes, so it is the same under every datum. Omitted when CO-OPS publishes no value for the month.

mn.description: Mean range of tide, MHW − MLW (MN), in the requested units. A difference between two tidal planes, so it is the same under every datum. Omitted when CO-OPS publishes no value for the month.

dhq.description: Mean diurnal high water inequality, MHHW − MHW (DHQ), in the requested units. A difference between two tidal planes, so it is the same under every datum. Omitted when CO-OPS publishes no value for the month.

dlq.description: Mean diurnal low water inequality, MLW − MLLW (DLQ), in the requested units. A difference between two tidal planes, so it is the same under every datum. Omitted when CO-OPS publishes no value for the month.

hwi.description: Greenwich high water interval (HWI), in hours. Omitted when CO-OPS publishes no value for the month.

lwi.description: Greenwich low water interval (LWI), in hours. Omitted when CO-OPS publishes no value for the month.

lowest.description: The month's lowest observed water level, in the requested units relative to the requested datum. Omitted when CO-OPS publishes no value for the month.

inferred.description: CO-OPS inferred-data code for the month, exactly as CO-OPS sends it. Observed values include "0", "1", and "11" — a code, not a boolean.

items.description: One station-month of tidal datums and extremes.

months.description: One row per station-month in the requested range, oldest first — the whole matched series when it fits one response, otherwise the leading page starting at offset. rows_matched and next_offset report what a page left behind.

notice.description: What this page of the monthly series covers and how to reach the next page.

truncated.description: True when this page stops short of the last matched month, so further months remain at next_offset. False on the final page and on a page past the end. Absent when the whole matched series was returned.

rows_matched.description: Months the requested range matched, before the page was cut. Absent when the whole matched series was returned.

rows_returned.description: Months this page carries — the length of months. Absent when the whole matched series was returned.

page_offset.description: Month offset this page starts at, echoed from the request. Absent when the whole matched series was returned.

next_offset.description: Offset to pass as offset on the next call, or null when this page reaches the last matched month. Absent when the whole matched series was returned.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_date_range`: begin_date or end_date is not a real calendar date, or the range starts after it ends. `date_range_exceeded`: The requested range spans more than 73,000 days, the CO-OPS limit for monthly means. `station_not_found`: CO-OPS rejected the station ID as not a valid station. `datum_unavailable`: The station does not carry the requested datum — a Great Lakes station has no tidal datum, and IGLD and LWD apply at Great Lakes stations only. `verified_data_lag`: CO-OPS returned no months for a window ending on or after the first day of the prior month, which it may not have verified yet. `no_data`: CO-OPS returned no months for a window ending before the prior month — the station has no monthly means for it. `upstream_throttled`: CO-OPS answered the monthly-mean request with HTTP 403, which it returns for about two minutes while it throttles a burst of requests from one address. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

events.description: Max flood, max ebb, and slack events — the whole matched series when it fits one response, otherwise the leading page starting at offset. Present for MAX_SLACK interval, and empty when CO-OPS answered with a statement instead of events — read notice for its wording.

time.description: Event datetime in the requested time zone.

type.description: Current event type: flood (onshore/inbound flow), ebb (offshore/outbound flow), or slack (near-zero current).

speed.description: Peak speed as a non-negative magnitude, in the requested units. Absent when CO-OPS reports no speed for the event, which is the usual case at slack water — though a slack event can carry a small residual speed under metric units.

direction.description: The station's mean flood direction on a flood event and its mean ebb direction on an ebb event, as a true bearing in degrees (0–360). A station constant, not an instantaneous heading. Absent for slack events and wherever CO-OPS reports no mean direction.

items.description: A single max flood, max ebb, or slack current event.

predictions.description: 6-minute continuous current predictions — the whole curve when it fits one response, otherwise the leading page starting at offset. Present for 6min interval, and empty when CO-OPS answered with a statement instead of a curve — read notice for its wording.

time.description: Prediction datetime in the requested time zone.

type.description: Flow sense at this row, from the sign of the speed CO-OPS predicts: flood (inbound), ebb (outbound), or slack (zero). speed is a non-negative magnitude, so this is what carries which way the water is moving.

speed.description: Current speed as a non-negative magnitude, in the requested units.

direction.description: The station's mean flood direction on a flood row and its mean ebb direction on an ebb row, as a true bearing in degrees (0–360). A station constant, not an instantaneous heading. Null on a slack row and wherever CO-OPS reports no mean direction.

notice.description: CO-OPS's own statement about the station when it returned that instead of prediction events — the answer to report, not a failure — or what this page of the prediction series covers and how to reach the next one.

truncated.description: True when this page stops short of the last matched row, so further rows remain at next_offset. False on the final page and on a page past the end. Absent when the whole matched series was returned.

rows_matched.description: Prediction rows the requested date range matched, before the page was cut. Absent when the whole matched series was returned.

rows_returned.description: Prediction rows this page carries — the length of events on the MAX_SLACK interval, of predictions on 6min. Absent when the whole matched series was returned.

page_offset.description: Row offset this page starts at, echoed from the request. Absent when the whole matched series was returned.

next_offset.description: Offset to pass as offset on the next call, or null when this page reaches the last matched row. Absent when the whole matched series was returned.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `station_not_found`: CO-OPS rejected the station ID as unknown or invalid — current stations require alphanumeric IDs. `invalid_date_range`: begin_date or end_date is not a real calendar date, or the range starts after it ends. `date_range_exceeded`: Requested date range exceeds the 1-year CO-OPS limit. `no_predictions`: Station exists but CO-OPS returned no current-prediction data for the requested date range. `predictions_unavailable`: The station is in the current-predictions catalog, but CO-OPS publishes no current predictions for it at any date. `bin_unavailable`: CO-OPS rejected the requested bin because the station publishes no predictions at that bin. `upstream_throttled`: CO-OPS answered HTTP 403, which it returns for about two minutes while it throttles a burst of requests from one address. success.description: Always true on a 200. Errors carry success:false and an error object.

id.description: Identifier for this verdict, safe to quote in a support request.

mode.description: You called this endpoint yourself, so the answer describes your own request.

keyDirectoryBinding.description: Whether your directory proved it published the key set that was read. binding-key-proven means the response signature verified but did not cover the body, so possession of the key is proven and the key set is not.

notes.description: Observations about your setup that are not faults.

knownBot.description: A second check, independent of the signature. Some operators publish the address ranges their crawlers use, and those lists are refreshed regularly. matched means the address this request came from is inside such a range. none is the usual answer and not a fault: no operator publishes a list containing this address, which holds for most agents and for every address that is not a large crawler.

refutedSignatures.description: Other signatures on the same request whose named directory does not list the key they used. You can confirm each against the published file yourself.

signature.description: Whether a Web Bot Auth signature was present and how it came out.

webBotAuthDetail.description: The specific fault, and the sentence saying what to change. Read this part first. Besides reason and fix it may carry three more members. clockDriftSec is how far the signing clock sits from this server, in seconds. directoryStatus is the HTTP status the named key directory answered with, where 403 or 429 is almost always a firewall in front of it refusing this verifier rather than anything about the keys. fromCachedDirectory appears only when true and means the answer rests on a stored copy that could not be refreshed, so a key reported as absent may simply have been published after that copy was taken.

card.description: Your own published card read back to you, plus the one promise a single live request can settle: the User-Agent you said you would send.

uaClient.description: What your User-Agent string alone says you are. A string, not a judgement.

clientHints.description: State of the Client Hints headers you sent.

provenance.description: measured = your request arrived directly and was read first-hand. unavailable = it did not, and no finding in this answer rests on it.

meta.description: Envelope: API version, how long the answer took, and the sources that contributed.

apiVersion.description: Version of this API, such as v1.

queryTimeMs.description: How long the answer took to build, in milliseconds.

axes.description: Sources that contributed to this answer, such as ip, knownBot and webBotAuth. A field can be missing without anything being wrong: its source did not contribute.

identity.description: Who you were established to be, and on what evidence. Empty of judgement: the outcome of checking a signature you sent against a directory you published.

operator.description: The name established for you, when one could be. Null when nothing named you.

bot.description: The specific bot within that operator, when the evidence distinguishes one.

method.description: How the name was established: signature when your own signature verified, ip-range when your address sat in a list its operator publishes.

trusted.description: Whether the established name is one this verifier holds a trust anchor for. A verified signature from an unknown domain still says who sent the request, and false here says that nothing more is known about that domain.

ip.description: Plain facts about your own address: network, operator, reputation of the address itself.

origin.description: What kind of network the address belongs to: residential, datacenter, mobile, and so on.

org.description: The organisation that network is registered to.

hostname.description: Reverse DNS name of the address, when it has one.

blacklisted.description: Whether the address appears on the public abuse feeds this service tracks.

riskScore.description: Reputation of the ADDRESS, 0 to 100, higher meaning worse. A datacenter address scores in the middle by nature: it is a statement about where you are, never about who you are or what you did.

title.description: Title as catalogued; empty when the museum lists none.

artist_display.description: Artist, nationality, and life dates as the museum displays them.

artist_id.description: Id of the preferred credited artist; pass as artist_id to artic_search_artworks.

date_display.description: Date as the museum displays it; the authority when the years are absent.

date_start.description: Earliest year of the date span, negative for BCE; omitted when absent or implausible.

date_end.description: Latest year of the date span, negative for BCE; omitted when absent or implausible.

artwork_type.description: Artwork type, such as Painting or Print.

is_public_domain.description: True when the work is public domain, so its images are CC0.

is_on_view.description: True when the work is on view at the museum now.

gallery.description: Gallery where the work is on view, such as Gallery 240.

web_url.description: Public page for the artwork on artic.edu.

image.description: Primary image with constructed IIIF URLs and its reuse status; absent when the work has no image.

url.description: IIIF image 843 px wide, the museum display size; available for every image, public domain or not.

url_large.description: IIIF image 1686 px wide; present only for public-domain works.

iiif_info_url.description: IIIF info.json URL listing the image dimensions, sizes, and tiles.

alt_text.description: Alt text the museum wrote for the image.

rights.description: Reuse status: public_domain images are CC0; in_copyright images need a rights check before reuse.

alt_titles.description: Other titles the work is known by.

main_reference_number.description: Museum reference (accession) number; empty when the museum lists none.

artist_ids.description: Ids of every credited artist; pass one as artist_id to artic_search_artworks.

date_qualifier.description: What the date marks, such as Made or Printed.

inscriptions.description: Inscriptions, signatures, and marks as catalogued.

credit_line.description: Credit line naming how the museum acquired the work.

edition.description: Edition statement for prints and multiples.

on_loan.description: Loan statement when the work is on loan.

manifest_url.description: IIIF Presentation manifest URL; present for public-domain works.

alt_images.description: Alternate images (other views, details); same rights as the primary image.

iiif_info_url.description: IIIF info.json URL for the image.

description.description: Curatorial description, CC BY 4.0: credit the Art Institute of Chicago and cite web_url. Present when the description section was requested and the museum wrote one.

short_description.description: Short curatorial description, attributed like description; returned with the description section.

provenance.description: Ownership history; returned with the provenance section.

exhibition_history.description: Exhibitions the work has appeared in; returned with the exhibition_history section.

publication_history.description: Publications citing the work; returned with the publication_history section.

catalogue.description: Catalogue raisonne entries; returned with the catalogue section.

related_media.description: Related multimedia (lectures, audio stops) from the museum; present when requested and at least one linked item loaded, never an empty list.

title.description: Asset title; empty when the museum lists none.

type.description: Asset type, such as sound.

artworks.description: Records in request order; ids the museum does not have are left out.

missing_ids.description: Attempted ids with no artwork, in request order; unattempted ids are not reported as missing.

deferred_ids.description: Ids left out by the response budget or beyond the first 10 attempted ids, in request order; pass them to artic_get_artworks again.

license_text.description: License statement from the API for this data, verbatim.

description_attribution.description: Attribution owed for description text (CC BY 4.0); present when any is returned.

notice.description: Guidance when ids are missing or deferred, or related media was capped or could not load.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `rate_limited`: The Art Institute API throttled this server and retries ran out, or the shared request queue could not start the call in time. `request_blocked`: The Art Institute API's firewall blocked the request, as it does for markup or script-like text and for bursts of traffic. `upstream_rejected_query`: The Art Institute API rejected a request this server built from valid inputs. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

summary.description: What the customer has answered, to read back to them for confirmation. Present only once `ready_to_quote` is true; null while there are still questions to ask.

quote_id.description: Pass this back to get_quote to read the result again.

more_carriers_pending.description: True when more carriers may still return a price; the list is not final.

poll_after_seconds.description: How long to wait before calling get_quote again.

pending_note.description: What to do while carriers are still answering, in the customer's language. Null once the list is final.

available.description: True once there are prices. There is always a next step towards the final quote.

next_call.description: Exactly what to call next, with its arguments: `next_question` with stage second_round while the application is incomplete; `carrier_questions` with `quote_id` (this quote) and `chosen_quote_id` (the `quote_id` of the estimate the customer picked) once it is, or with no `chosen_quote_id` when `firm_prices` is present. Null before there are prices.

note.description: What to tell the customer, in their language.

price_may_change.description: One line on what finishing can do to the price, in the customer's language. It never promises a better price, and never mentions a carrier that has not answered.

status.description: rating: carriers still answering. questions_pending: ask carrier_questions with this quote_id and no chosen_quote_id. pricing: the carriers are confirming; options holds what has landed, read again after poll_after_seconds. ready: every price is in options and the customer chooses and pays in the link. agent: no carrier confirmed a price online; a Sigo agent takes it.

due_today.description: What the customer pays today, broker fee included.

installment_amount.description: Per instalment after today; null for pay-in-full.

total_for_term.description: Today's payment plus the instalments. Stated so it is not worked out.

payment_method.description: The way of paying this price is valid on: card, ach or direct_bill. The customer confirms it in the link.

roadside_included.description: Whether roadside assistance is part of this price.

requires_autopay.description: True when this price is only available with automatic payments. Say so with the price; the customer accepts autopay in the link before paying it.

excluded_people.description: How many people the carrier excluded from this price. Say so with the price when it is not zero; who they are is shown in the link, never here.

options.description: The firm prices the customer may pay now, lowest today's payment first. Each is a carrier's confirmed price, still subject to underwriting, eligibility, and state filing, and bought only in the link.

poll_after_seconds.description: While pricing: how long to wait before get_quote again.

next_call.description: Exactly what to call next, with its arguments; null when nothing is.

note.description: What to tell the customer and do next, in their language.

complete.description: True when the application has everything RC3 needs. False while anything is missing.

still_needed.description: What is missing, empty when nothing is. Null on a quote issued before this was recorded, where completeness is unknown rather than proven.

note.description: What to do about it, in the customer's language.

carrier_name.description: The carrier that issues this policy. Sigo is the agency, not the issuer.

due_today.description: What the customer pays today to start the policy. Not the policy total.

first_payment_note.description: What the amount due today is, in words the customer hears. It is stated for every estimate, whichever of the two numbers is larger.

total_for_term.description: What the payment plan adds up to over the term: the amount due today plus every instalment. Stated rather than left to be worked out — an agent asked for the six-month total produced one of its own.

total_note.description: What that total is and what it does not include. It travels with the number for the same reason the first payment's note does: a trailing sentence gets paraphrased away.

term_months.description: Policy term in months, or null when the carrier did not report one. A 6-month and a 12-month quote are not comparable on the down payment alone, so do not rank on price without it.

quote_type.description: Always an estimate, in every round. No price the connector returns is final: the final quote is calculated by Sigo in the link, after the carrier's questions and before the customer pays.

text.description: The notice, in the customer's language.

show_verbatim.description: This text goes to the customer as it is written, in the same answer as the price. It is short enough to fit: shortening it further drops the disclosure Sigo is required to make, and a summary of it is not that disclosure. It carries no instructions to the model and none to the customer.

next_step.description: Where the customer continues with Sigo — present only once the list of prices is final. While carriers are still answering it is null, because a customer cannot choose from a list that is still filling.

message.description: Customer-safe wording. Upstream carrier or configuration detail is never included.

phone_collected_here.description: No phone number reaches this connector: the input schema has no field for one.

sigo_calls_customers.description: Sigo's agents do call and text customers. What cannot happen is a call arranged from here, because this channel never has a number to call.

url.description: Where the customer leaves a phone number for a Sigo agent. Present as soon as the list is final, whether or not anything was quoted; null only while carriers are still answering. This is the only way on from here — do not offer another.

note.description: What to say when the customer asks to be called, in their language.
Present from two vehicles up: say it with the prices, because one amount for a household reads as an amount per car. Null for a single vehicle, where the amount can only mean one thing.

position.description: 1-based, in the order start_quote received them.

deductible.description: Null for liability, or when none was given.

vehicles.description: Empty on a quote started before this field existed; then the agent's own record is the label.

asked_for.description: Label each answer with this when comparing two quotes for the same customer, so "con deducible de 1000" is matched to the quote that asked for it.

revised_from_quote.description: True when this quote re-quoted the same customer: started with revise_of, or for a customer who already quoted today and was still at their first round. One person, one application, priced again.

available.description: The only changes worth offering, and they re-quote: empty when this quote has none, and then the honest answer is that there is nothing to adjust at this step.

note.description: How to answer the question, in the customer's language.

personal_use_note.description: Present when the customer said the vehicle is used for work. Say it with the prices: this quote is personal auto. Null when they said nothing about it, and then the subject is not raised.

answered.description: The carriers that returned a price for this quote, and the only ones that may be named.

catalogue_is_public.description: Sigo publishes no list of the carriers it works with: it varies by state and by quote, and cannot be derived from this response. A carrier absent from `answered` is not thereby a carrier Sigo does not work with.

note.description: What may be said about carriers, in the customer's language.

charges_broker_fee.description: Whether Sigo charges this customer a broker fee, which depends on their state. True: a fee for the agency's service, on top of a commission from the carrier. False: Sigo charges them no fee at all. Either way it is not part of the amounts in this response — those are the carrier's — and cannot be derived from them: where there is one, it is itemised for the customer before purchase. An estimate is not the final cost of buying through Sigo.

available.description: True once there are prices. There is always a next step towards the final quote.

next_call.description: Exactly what to call next, with its arguments: `next_question` with stage second_round while the application is incomplete; `carrier_questions` with `quote_id` (this quote) and `chosen_quote_id` (the `quote_id` of the estimate the customer picked) once it is, or with no `chosen_quote_id` when `firm_prices` is present. Null before there are prices.

note.description: What to tell the customer, in their language.

price_may_change.description: One line on what finishing can do to the price, in the customer's language. It never promises a better price, and never mentions a carrier that has not answered.

status.description: rating: carriers still answering. questions_pending: ask carrier_questions with this quote_id and no chosen_quote_id. pricing: the carriers are confirming; options holds what has landed, read again after poll_after_seconds. ready: every price is in options and the customer chooses and pays in the link. agent: no carrier confirmed a price online; a Sigo agent takes it.

due_today.description: What the customer pays today, broker fee included.

installment_amount.description: Per instalment after today; null for pay-in-full.

total_for_term.description: Today's payment plus the instalments. Stated so it is not worked out.

payment_method.description: The way of paying this price is valid on: card, ach or direct_bill. The customer confirms it in the link.

roadside_included.description: Whether roadside assistance is part of this price.

requires_autopay.description: True when this price is only available with automatic payments. Say so with the price; the customer accepts autopay in the link before paying it.

excluded_people.description: How many people the carrier excluded from this price. Say so with the price when it is not zero; who they are is shown in the link, never here.

options.description: The firm prices the customer may pay now, lowest today's payment first. Each is a carrier's confirmed price, still subject to underwriting, eligibility, and state filing, and bought only in the link.

poll_after_seconds.description: While pricing: how long to wait before get_quote again.

next_call.description: Exactly what to call next, with its arguments; null when nothing is.

note.description: What to tell the customer and do next, in their language.

complete.description: True when the application has everything RC3 needs. False while anything is missing.

still_needed.description: What is missing, empty when nothing is. Null on a quote issued before this was recorded, where completeness is unknown rather than proven.

note.description: What to do about it, in the customer's language.

carrier_name.description: The carrier that issues this policy. Sigo is the agency, not the issuer.

due_today.description: What the customer pays today to start the policy. Not the policy total.

first_payment_note.description: What the amount due today is, in words the customer hears. It is stated for every estimate, whichever of the two numbers is larger.

total_for_term.description: What the payment plan adds up to over the term: the amount due today plus every instalment. Stated rather than left to be worked out — an agent asked for the six-month total produced one of its own.

total_note.description: What that total is and what it does not include. It travels with the number for the same reason the first payment's note does: a trailing sentence gets paraphrased away.

term_months.description: Policy term in months, or null when the carrier did not report one. A 6-month and a 12-month quote are not comparable on the down payment alone, so do not rank on price without it.

quote_type.description: Always an estimate, in every round. No price the connector returns is final: the final quote is calculated by Sigo in the link, after the carrier's questions and before the customer pays.

text.description: The notice, in the customer's language.

show_verbatim.description: This text goes to the customer as it is written, in the same answer as the price. It is short enough to fit: shortening it further drops the disclosure Sigo is required to make, and a summary of it is not that disclosure. It carries no instructions to the model and none to the customer.

next_step.description: Where the customer continues with Sigo — present only once the list of prices is final. While carriers are still answering it is null, because a customer cannot choose from a list that is still filling.

message.description: Customer-safe wording. Upstream carrier or configuration detail is never included.

phone_collected_here.description: No phone number reaches this connector: the input schema has no field for one.

sigo_calls_customers.description: Sigo's agents do call and text customers. What cannot happen is a call arranged from here, because this channel never has a number to call.

url.description: Where the customer leaves a phone number for a Sigo agent. Present as soon as the list is final, whether or not anything was quoted; null only while carriers are still answering. This is the only way on from here — do not offer another.

note.description: What to say when the customer asks to be called, in their language.
Present from two vehicles up: say it with the prices, because one amount for a household reads as an amount per car. Null for a single vehicle, where the amount can only mean one thing.

position.description: 1-based, in the order start_quote received them.

deductible.description: Null for liability, or when none was given.

vehicles.description: Empty on a quote started before this field existed; then the agent's own record is the label.

asked_for.description: Label each answer with this when comparing two quotes for the same customer, so "con deducible de 1000" is matched to the quote that asked for it.

revised_from_quote.description: True when this quote re-quoted the same customer: started with revise_of, or for a customer who already quoted today and was still at their first round. One person, one application, priced again.

available.description: The only changes worth offering, and they re-quote: empty when this quote has none, and then the honest answer is that there is nothing to adjust at this step.

note.description: How to answer the question, in the customer's language.

personal_use_note.description: Present when the customer said the vehicle is used for work. Say it with the prices: this quote is personal auto. Null when they said nothing about it, and then the subject is not raised.

answered.description: The carriers that returned a price for this quote, and the only ones that may be named.

catalogue_is_public.description: Sigo publishes no list of the carriers it works with: it varies by state and by quote, and cannot be derived from this response. A carrier absent from `answered` is not thereby a carrier Sigo does not work with.

note.description: What may be said about carriers, in the customer's language.

charges_broker_fee.description: Whether Sigo charges this customer a broker fee, which depends on their state. True: a fee for the agency's service, on top of a commission from the carrier. False: Sigo charges them no fee at all. Either way it is not part of the amounts in this response — those are the carrier's — and cannot be derived from them: where there is one, it is itemised for the customer before purchase. An estimate is not the final cost of buying through Sigo.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `scope_filter_mismatch`: A filter was combined with a scope, municipality, or language that does not support it, or mutually exclusive version filters were combined — rejected locally before any upstream call; the message names the offending pair. `invalid_query`: A page past the last page of results, or RIS rejecting a parameter value in-band — the Client error message is passed through verbatim, in German. It names the invalid element and its valid values, except for a page past the end, which names no parameter at all. Unsupported filter combinations are caught earlier as scope_filter_mismatch. `upstream_error`: RIS is unreachable, returned a server error, or served an HTML error page. `upstream_timeout`: RIS did not answer the search within the request deadline. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `scope_filter_mismatch`: A filter was combined with a scope that does not support it (part off federal; series/state_era off a state scope; district_authority off district; municipality off municipal; issuer outside federal/ordinance gazettes), or series: ordinance_gazette was combined with state_era: legacy (ordinance gazettes have no legacy counterpart) — rejected locally before any upstream call; the message names the offending pair. `cross_tier_range`: A federal published_from/published_to interval overlaps more than one Bundesgesetzblatt era tier (BgblAuth 2004+, BgblPdf 1945–2003, BgblAlt 1848–1940) — including a one-sided bound, which is open into every tier beyond it. Rejected locally before any upstream call: one call serves exactly one application, so a spanning range would return the records of a single tier and silently omit the rest of the interval. A year-bearing number or part: pre_1997 names the tier outright and is never rejected. `unresolved_ministry`: A federal issuer is an abbreviation-shaped value matching no row of the RIS ministries table (the message names the closest matches), or a ministry the table lists only for another issuer parameter (the message names the parameters that accept it) — rejected locally before any upstream call. A value the table does not know that contains a space is sent to RIS as written instead. `invalid_query`: A page past the last page of results; or a parameter the resolved gazette does not carry — sort_by, number, type, part, issuer, or a state absent from the historical Lgbl series — rejected locally before any upstream call, naming the field and the gazette that rejected it (by scope/series/state_era, or for a federal era tier by its window and the input that routed there); or RIS rejecting a value in-band (the Client error message is passed through verbatim, in German, and it does not name the page). `upstream_error`: RIS is unreachable, returned a server error, or served an HTML error page. `upstream_timeout`: RIS did not answer the search within the request deadline. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `upstream_error`: A routed RIS search was unreachable, returned a server error, or served an HTML error page. An unparseable or unresolvable citation is NOT this error — it returns found: false. `upstream_timeout`: A routed RIS search did not answer within the request deadline. tools.name: ris_get_document
tools.why: declared schema rejects the corrupted payload

text.description: The document text in the requested format. Absent for urls_only, when the application carries no text rendition (see the notice), for an outline (kind: outline), and for an html or xml rendition over the 40,000-byte budget (kind: link).

format.description: The format served — echoes the requested format.

byte_size.description: Full UTF-8 byte size of the document text. Present when text was fetched — for an overflowed document (kind: outline) or an over-budget html/xml rendition (kind: link) this reports the full text’s size, not the returned payload’s.

truncated.description: Present and true when the full text isn’t inline. kind: outline — the markdown overflowed the byte budget or a sections:[…] selector matched nothing (the notice names which); retrieve entries via the sections input. kind: link — an html or xml rendition overflowed the budget; fetch content_urls.html or content_urls.xml for the whole artifact, or re-call with format: markdown.

kind.description: full — the complete response (document text, selected entries, or rendition URLs). outline — sections lists the retrievable entries instead of the text, either because the markdown overflowed the byte budget or because a sections:[…] selector matched nothing; re-call with sections:[…] naming entries from it. link — an html or xml rendition over the 40,000-byte budget: no text, only byte_size and content_urls, whose entry for the requested format fetches the whole artifact in one GET; re-call with format: markdown to read it.

sections.description: Present when kind = outline: the document’s addressable entries, each with its UTF-8 byte size — §/Artikel/Anlage sections listed largest first, or, when the markdown carries no such headings, Part n of N byte windows listed in document order and summing to byte_size. Copy names into the sections input verbatim to retrieve them; naming several in one call returns their text concatenated in document order, with nothing inserted between them.

name.description: Section identifier — pass in `sections` to retrieve it

bytes.description: Serialized byte size of the section

items.description: A retrievable entry — a §/Artikel/Anlage section or a Part n of N byte window, with its UTF-8 byte size.

binding_status.description: Legal binding status: authentic (amtssigniert, legally binding), consolidated_informational (consolidated view — not binding), historical_record (superseded/pre-e-Recht promulgation), decision (court/tribunal ruling), preparatory (draft/bill/minutes), administrative_directive (binds the administration, not citizens), or translation (unofficial English).

content_urls.description: Constructed rendition URLs. Empty for authentic-PDF-only (Bvb/GrA/KmGer) and metadata-only (BgblAlt) applications — see authentic_pdf_url and the notice. For a companion document (a draft’s Erläuterungen, Textgegenüberstellung, WFA, cover letter, or annex) these are the companion’s own XML/HTML/PDF, not the parent document’s — constructed rather than read back from RIS, so for the roughly one companion in eight that RIS files as a PDF only, xml and html return 404 and pdf is the one that resolves.

authentic_pdf_url.description: The amtssigniert authentic PDF (.pdfsig, Authentisch DataType) — the legally binding artifact — where the application publishes one.

application.description: RIS application the document belongs to (echoed).

notice.description: Present when the requested text format is unavailable for this application (names why and the usable URL), when the document overflowed to a section outline (names how to retrieve sections), when an html or xml rendition overflowed to a link (names content_urls.<format> and format: markdown), or when a sections:[…] entry matched no section or was ignored (names the unmatched entries).

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_addressing`: Neither or both addressing modes were provided, document_number was given without application, or the document_number/application pairing is not a valid RIS document — thrown locally before any fetch. `unsupported_url`: document_url fails the origin + /Dokumente/ path-prefix allowlist (exactly https://www.ris.bka.gv.at and https://ogd.ris.bka.gv.at), its path segment is not a recognized RIS application, or its trailing filename addresses neither the document’s own rendition nor one of its companion documents — thrown locally, nothing fetched. `document_not_found`: The constructed or passed content URL returned 404. `upstream_error`: The RIS content host was unreachable or returned a server error. `upstream_timeout`: The content host did not return the rendition within the fetch deadline — typically a cold render, which it performs on first request before caching the result. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

document_url.description: RIS web view of the document (Allgemein.DokumentUrl) — for humans.

binding_status.description: Legal binding status of the queried application — authentic (amtssigniert, legally binding), consolidated_informational, historical_record, decision, preparatory, administrative_directive, or translation.

deleted.description: True when this record marks a document removed from RIS (include_deleted only).

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Collections use LIST<T> and MAP<K,V>, for example LIST<STRING> or MAP<STRING,OrderStatus>. Container nesting and PAGE fields are not supported. FILE is allowed only as a direct field type; TEXT cannot be a map value. Map keys are BOOLEAN, STRING, INTEGER, LONG, DOUBLE, UUID or an enum name.

max.description: Maximum length for STRING or LIST<STRING> fields

precision.description: Total decimal digits for NUMERIC or LIST<NUMERIC> fields

scale.description: Fractional decimal digits for NUMERIC or LIST<NUMERIC>; must not exceed precision

fileEndings.description: Allowed file endings for FILE fields

fields.description: Complete ordered entity field list. Exactly one primary key is required for a concrete entity unless inherited; abstract superclasses may omit it. A primary key must be the first field and use INTEGER, LONG, UUID or STRING. required is ignored for it.

relations.description: Present when RELATIONS is requested in details. Each identifier is the canonical selector for the current state and must be copied into updateRelation or deleteRelation. Refetch after renaming an entity or changing an owning field.

type.description: Cardinality from fromEntity to toEntity

fromEntity.description: Entity on the from side of the cardinality

fromField.description: Field generated on fromEntity. Required unless an unidirectional ONE_TO_MANY relation omits this reverse field

toEntity.description: Entity on the to side of the cardinality

toField.description: Field generated on toEntity. Required for ONE_TO_MANY and bidirectional relations; also required for self-referencing MANY_TO_MANY relations

tableName.description: Join-table name; required only for MANY_TO_MANY

required.description: Whether the owning foreign key is required. Not applicable to MANY_TO_MANY or self-relations

unidirectional.description: Omit the reverse field. Relations across application modules must be unidirectional

identifier.description: Canonical relation selector. It is OwningEntity.owningField: fromEntity.fromField for MANY_TO_ONE, ONE_TO_ONE and MANY_TO_MANY, but toEntity.toField for ONE_TO_MANY. Copy this value into updateRelation or deleteRelation.

indexes.description: Present when INDEXES is requested in details

entity.description: Entity containing the indexed fields or owning-side relations

unique.description: Whether the index enforces a unique field combination

items.description: Entity field or owning-side relation name

fields.description: Ordered field or owning-side relation names. Order affects index usage; many-to-many relations are not available and a primary key cannot be used alone.

breakpointStatus.description: Present when BREAKPOINTS is requested. AVAILABLE means a new breakpoint is meaningful; NO_SCHEMA and NO_CHANGES do not allow one; LIMIT_REACHED blocks further additions.

breakpoints.description: Present when BREAKPOINTS is requested. IDs are Unix epoch seconds in creation order.

restControllers.description: Present when REST_CONTROLLERS is requested in details. Available with Bootify Professional.

featurePackage.description: Optional dot-separated package path for domain-driven or mixed structure; null uses automatic assignment

entity.description: Source entity name for generated controllers

query.description: Whether the parameter originates from the query declaration

parameters.description: Parameters in path order; query is derived from the path declaration

path.description: Endpoint path. Declare path parameters as {name} and query parameters as ?name=&other=, then provide matching name and type entries in parameters.

inputType.description: Required for POST, PUT and PATCH; omit for other HTTP methods. Types: VOID, BOOLEAN, STRING, INTEGER, LONG, DOUBLE, UUID, or an existing project enum or data object name, including entity-generated DTOs. No collections. Custom types must be accessible from the controller module.

responseType.description: Types: VOID, BOOLEAN, STRING, INTEGER, LONG, DOUBLE, UUID, or an existing project enum or data object name, including entity-generated DTOs. VOID means no response body. Collections: LIST<T>, PAGE<T>, MAP<K,V>; no nesting. Map keys: BOOLEAN, STRING, INTEGER, LONG, DOUBLE, UUID or an enum. Custom types must be accessible from the controller module. Example: PAGE<OrderDTO>.

calc_definition_json.description: The compiled interview definition JSON (structure varies by interview type).

question.description: The question text shown to the candidate.

id.description: Identifier for this question. job-interview-get returns the question's real id here; send it back to job-interview-update so an unchanged question keeps its existing record (and with it its answer rules and any rendered avatar video). Also the handle another question references via conditional_question_main_id. On job-interview-create-from-array it is a caller-local value, only needed for those references.

duration.description: Answer duration in seconds for this question.

mojito_language_code.description: Per-question language override (one of the platform-languages.json codes). Inherits the interview language when omitted.

label.description: Optional label/tag stored on the question.

is_conditional.description: Conditional follow-up question (view 'with listening conditional'). Use with conditional_question_main_id.

is_without_scoring.description: Question is asked but not scored (view 'without scoring').

conditional_question_main_id.description: For a conditional question, the id (the "id" field above) of the parent question in this same array that triggers it. The parent must appear earlier in the array than the conditional question referencing it.

knowledge_base_id.description: Knowledge-base store id (uuid) the question draws context from.

external_id.description: External identifier stored on the question. job-interview-update matches on this first, so an ATS that owns stable ids can send its own array and have the diff line up without round-tripping our ids.

external_data.description: Arbitrary JSON metadata stored on the question.

weak.description: Baseline requirements every viable candidate should meet (table stakes).

moderate.description: Requirements expected of a solid, competent candidate.

strong.description: High-bar requirements only standout candidates clear.

candidate_expectations_json.description: Per-question candidate expectations, bucketed by requirement level (weak/moderate/strong). Extra keys are preserved.

questions.description: The interview questions, in the order they are asked, in the same format job-interview-create-from-array accepts — so this array can be edited and sent straight back to job-interview-update, or used to create a copy of this interview. Each `id` is the question's real identifier: send it back unchanged and the question keeps its existing record (and with it its answer rules and any rendered avatar video). The welcome, thank-you and instructional-video steps are NOT included — they are not questions in this format, and job-interview-update leaves them untouched. Null for multi-stage positions, whose questions live on the individual interview stages.

is_multistage.description: True when the id resolved to a multi-stage position rather than a single interview.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the interview/position.

visibility.description: Who can see and access the interview/position.

stage.description: Hiring-pipeline stage. Null for multi-stage positions.

type.description: Interview type. Null for multi-stage positions.

environment.description: Which webhook environment this interview's results are delivered to. Null for multi-stage positions, whose stages each carry their own.

code.description: Caller-supplied external code/reference.

interview_template_id.description: Interview template id. For multi-stage positions this is the first interview step's template.

interview_template_type.description: Type of the linked interview template. `interactive_elevenlabs` is voice-only; the others (`interactive_spatius`, `interactive_heygen`, `offline_heygen`, `offline_elai`, `offline_synthesia`) are avatar-based. Null when the template could not be resolved.

is_voice_only.description: Convenience flag derived from interview_template_type: true when voice-only (`interactive_elevenlabs`), false when avatar-based, null when the template type could not be resolved.

knowledge_base_store_id.description: Linked knowledge base store id. Null for multi-stage positions.

speech_language_code.description: Azure speech language code. Null for multi-stage positions.

speech_language_name.description: Azure speech language display name. Null for multi-stage positions.

recording.description: Per-answer recording mode. Null for multi-stage positions.

recording_full_session.description: Full-session recording mode. Null for multi-stage positions.

type_credit.description: Credit bucket the interview draws from. Null for multi-stage positions.

result_view.description: Result view level. Null for multi-stage positions.

Alongside normal Markdown you can place these directives, each ALONE on its own line: `[plan-progress]` (the learner's coaching-plan progress), `[directory:<tag-id>]` (a card for one sub-directory), `[session:<interview-id>]` (a card for one session), `[sessions]` (every session in this directory), `[sessions:<term>]` (sessions matching a term), `[sessions:filter=<term>,limit=<n>]` (a filtered, capped list). score.description: BM25 relevance: each query term is weighted by how RARE it is in this corpus and by where it hits (name 3, tags 2, questions 2, body 1). A hit must also cover a minimum share of the question's information, measured in the same rarity weights — matching only common words does not qualify. Centrality (how many objects point at this one) breaks TIES ONLY and is never part of the score, so it cannot make an irrelevant object rank. Two hits with the same matched_fields can still differ: the score is rarity-weighted, so matching a rare term is worth more than matching a common one.

matched_fields.description: Which fields the query hit: name, tags, questions, summary, claims. Does NOT determine the score on its own.

coverage.description: Share of the question's information this object accounts for, weighted by term rarity. 1 means every meaningful word in the query is present; a low value with a high score means the object matched common words only.

outputSchema.description: The single-claim response served at GET /api/claims/{id}.

Argument.description: One side of a Dossier (pro or con).

aboard:operator.description: The accountable human or organisation behind the credential that filed this content. Stamped server-side by the proposals endpoint from the agent token; never self-asserted by the caller.

aboard:agentId.description: Stable identifier for the agent configuration (model + prompt + tool stack), as distinct from schema:name, which is a free-form label. Also stamped server-side.

schema:question.description: The historical question — 'how often has X happened in similar setups?'

ClaimKind.description: Three categories. Symptoms are observed harms; mechanisms are causal pathways; leverage points are interventions.

ContextObject.description: JSON-LD @context object used by every aboard response. Maps the two short prefixes 'schema' and 'aboard' to their full vocabularies.

Crux.description: A pivot claim within a Dossier whose resolution would settle the debate.

DataPoint.description: A quantitative observation that backs a claim. Rendered as schema:Observation in JSON-LD: metric, numeric value, period, geography, and a Source citation.

schema:measuredProperty.description: The metric being measured, e.g. 'Top 1% income share, US'.

Dossier.description: A non-convergent dual-thesis debate attached to a contested claim.

Edge.description: A directed relation between two claims. Always carries a rationale; may carry citations supporting the claimed relation.

aboard:rationale.description: Free-text explanation of the claimed relation. Required: relations are classified on stated reasoning, not on edge counts.

aboard:resolutionSource.description: The external, real-world dataset or publication that resolves this forecast. Optional while the corpus backfills; absence means the forecast has no anchor outside the graph yet.

aboard:resolvedOutcome.description: How the forecast resolved. Absent means not resolved yet; an explicit null means resolved as annulled and excluded from scoring. Binary outcomes map to 1/0 for proper scoring; the numeric arm is reserved for range questions.

aboard:resolvedAt.description: When the forecast was resolved. Present whenever aboard:resolvedOutcome is.

aboard:supersededBy.description: References to the forecasts that replace this one. A forecast with under-specified criteria is never edited in place — that would change what its existing predictions were answering — so the repair is new forecasts, named here. The superseded forecast stays filed as historical record and is excluded from resolution-criteria linting.

by_outcome_linked_to_object_of_search.description: Matched stops by whether the outcome was linked to the object of search ('true', 'false' or '(not recorded)'), most first.

by_removal_of_more_than_outer_clothing.description: Matched stops by whether more than outer clothing was removed ('true', 'false' or '(not recorded)' where the force sent no value, as some do for vehicle-only searches), most first.

type.description: Person search, vehicle search, or both.

self_defined_ethnicity.description: Ethnicity as the person defined it.

officer_defined_ethnicity.description: Ethnicity as the officer perceived it.

legislation.description: Power the search was made under.

truncated.description: True when more rows remain after this page.

notice.description: Defaulted month, coverage gaps, why a result is empty, and how to page on.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_area`: the area's required fields are missing, or a field it does not use is present. `month_not_published`: month or month_from is after the latest published month. `month_out_of_range`: month or month_from is before the 36-month window. `invalid_month_range`: month_from is after month, or the range spans more than 12 months. `unknown_force`: force matches no listed force id or name, or more than one, or is 'btp' on area 'neighbourhood'. `unknown_neighbourhood`: the force has no neighbourhood with this id (ids are case-sensitive). `area_too_large`: the area holds more stops than data.police.uk will answer for. `range_too_large`: the range's months hold more records than one call keeps for a range. `range_incomplete`: the months of the range could not all be fetched within the time one call allows. `upstream_unavailable`: data.police.uk is not answering. `rate_limited`: data.police.uk is rate-limiting this server for longer than this call can wait. `pacer_shed`: too many requests to data.police.uk are already queued in this server. `retry_deadline_exceeded`: data.police.uk did not answer within the time one call allows. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.
